Upon investigation, chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court. Date: GUPTA 2024.10.28 04:08:28 +0530 MACT No: 116/2017 Bharat v. Akhilesh & ors. P.No. 2 of 25 ss 4. MACT No: 116/2017 Bharat v. Akhilesh & ors. P.No. 3 of 25 ss in a road traffic accident dated 01.10.2014 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. GJ-09Y-9479 driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3 ?
texts.arguments: It is argued on behalf of petitioner that the petitioner has proved the occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending truck. He has proved suffering of grievous injury and permanent physical impairment/ disability of 85% in relation to whole body. It is argued that since the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3, such insurance company is liable to compensate the petitioner. On the other hand, it is argued on behalf of the insurance company that since it is an admitted fact that the petitioner was triple riding a motorcycle and conducted himself in a way endangering his life and safety, he was solely responsible for the accident. Further, since the owner and insurer of the motorcycle that met with the accident have not been impleaded as parties, the present claim is bad for non joinder. It is further argued that the petitioner has failed to examine himself or any other eye witness to the accident and therefore, his claim cannot be said to have been proved in accordance with law. It is further argued that the driver of the motorbike on which petitioner was a pillion rider, was also not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, insurance company of the offending vehicle cannot be made liable to compensate the petitioner. She has categorically deposed that the accident was a head on collision with the offending vehicle which suddenly came from the wrong side of the road from the opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner. The primary defence raised by Ld. counsel for insurance company is regarding non examination of the injured himself and his plea that the witness examined by the petitioner is not an eye witness to the accident. At the same time, it is the plea raised by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that the petitioner has suffered 85% of permanent disability including neurological impairment of his faculties due to which petitioner could not have deposed before the court as a competent witness. The petitioner has to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, the occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
